summary: Joseph S. Alter works in Indology, religious studies, and other fields. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, and was attested as a professor at the University of Pittsburgh in 2008.

Joseph Tiefenthaler was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. A Jesuit missionary with the Society of Jesus from 1729 to 1773, he served as rector of Agra Jesuit College around 1744 to 1747.

Joseph Toussaint Reinaud studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held positions at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, held a chair at INALCO from 1838, and served as president of the Société Asiatique from 1847 to 1867.

Linguist Joseph Vendryes studied under Antoine Meillet, Victor Henry, Sylvain Lévi, and Rudolf Thurneysen. He taught at the University of Paris from 1907 to 1946, the École Normale Supérieure (1920–1936), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1926–1952).

Joseph Virgil Grohmann, active in Indology and linguistics, earned his PhD at Charles University studying under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He served as a professor at Prager Handelsakademie and later directed the Leitmeritzer Oberrealschule.

Joseph Walker Jasper Ouseley was an Indologist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He was a professor at Fort William College, taught Arabic and Persian at East India Company College (1844–1859), and examined for the Civil Service Commission.
Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Joseph Walser studied under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenberg, and David S. Pacini. He was attested at Loyola University Chicago in 1998.

Linguist Joseph Wright earned his PhD at Heidelberg University under Hermann Osthoff, also studying at Yorkshire College and Leipzig. He lectured at the University of Oxford before serving as Professor of Comparative Philology at Corpus Christi College, Oxford (1901–1925).

Joseph van den Gheyn studied under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin at KU Leuven, where he later taught. Active in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies, he held a chair at the Institut Catholique de Paris and served at the BnF.

Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen and was associated with the Austrian Academy of Sciences from around 1847 to 1856.
Josho Nozawa worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying under Susumu Yamaguchi. He was attested as a professor at Koyasan University in 1950.

Joshu Sasaki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Zuiryo-ji under Joten Soko Miura. He served as abbot at Yotoku-in and Shojuan, founded the Mount Baldy Zen Center, and served as its abbot until 2012.
Joshua Ereshefsky works in Buddhist and religious studies. Attested in 2026, he pursued a PhD in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn.
Joshua Marshman was a scholar of Indology, Sinology, and linguistics who studied at Bristol Baptist College and under Johannes Lassar. In 1818, he founded Serampore College.

Linguist Joshua Timothy Katz studied at Yale, Oxford, and Harvard. He was the Cotsen Professor in the Humanities at Princeton University (1998–2022) and became a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute around 2022.
Joshua W. C. Cutler, active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied under Geshe Wangyal. He was attested at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center in 2004.

Linguist Joshua Whatmough studied at the University of Manchester and Emmanuel College. He taught classics at Bangor University (1921–1925), served as Professor of Latin at Cairo University (1925–1926), and became a professor at Harvard University in 1926.

Philosopher Josiah Royce studied at the University of California, Berkeley, under Hermann Lotze at Göttingen, and at Johns Hopkins. After an instructorship at Berkeley, he served on the Harvard University faculty from 1882 until 1916.

Josip Florschütz worked in linguistics and Indology, completing his PhD at the University of Vienna. In 1908, he became an extraordinary professor of comparative Indo-European linguistics, Sanskrit, Lithuanian, Gothic, and Albanian at the University of Zagreb.

José Alemany y Bolufer studied under Pedro Roca y López and completed degrees at Barcelona and Complutense University of Madrid. He served as professor of Greek at the University of Granada and later at Complutense University of Madrid (c. 1904–1934).
